aos.desc: Use and apply standard techniques: recall facts, use notation correctly and carry out routine and multi-step procedures.
Reason, interpret and communicate mathematically: make deductions, build chains of reasoning, argue and prove.
Solve problems within mathematics and in other contexts: translate problems, make connections, interpret and evaluate results.

commandWords.meaning: Find a numerical answer, showing the method.
Give enough working to reach a stated answer convincingly.
Give a logical argument, with justified steps, that a result is always true (Higher).
State why, using mathematical language or a rule.
Find the value or values of the unknown that satisfy the equation.
Rewrite an expression in the required algebraic form.
Use rounded values to find an approximate answer.
Show the key features of a graph or shape, with accuracy as the question requires.

gaps: Command words are not defined in the specification pages read; the list above uses the wording commonly seen in Edexcel papers and should be checked against the current Pearson mark schemes.
Question-style descriptions per paper are summarised generally; the exact wording of the specification at a glance table was read as a summary, not as a verbatim table.
Equipment supplied in the examination (for example mathematical instruments) is not stated in the specification content read.
Pearson may have published later issues of the specification or updated guidance since Issue 2 (June 2015); the live Pearson page should be checked before each academic year.

units.title: Number: structure and calculation
points: Order integers, decimals and fractions, including negatives, using the comparison symbols (N1).
Apply the four operations to integers, decimals and fractions of any sign, using place value (N2).
Use inverse operations, cancellation and the order of operations including powers, roots and reciprocals (N3).
Use primes, factors, multiples, HCF, LCM and prime factorisation (N4).
Apply systematic listing; at Higher also the product rule for counting (N5).
Use positive integer powers and real roots, and estimate powers and roots (N6).
Calculate with roots and integer indices; at Higher include fractional indices (N7).
Calculate exactly with fractions and multiples of pi; at Higher use and rationalise surds (N8).
Calculate with and interpret numbers in standard form (N9).

units.title: Number: fractions, decimals and percentages
points: Convert between terminating decimals and fractions; at Higher also recurring decimals (N10).
Work with fractions within ratio problems (N11).
Interpret and use fractions and percentages as operators (N12).

units.title: Number: measures and accuracy
points: Use standard units of measure, including compound measures (N13).
Estimate answers and check calculations, including those made with technology (N14).
Round to appropriate accuracy and use inequality notation for error intervals (N15).
Apply and interpret limits of accuracy; at Higher use upper and lower bounds (N16).

units.title: Algebra: notation, vocabulary and manipulation
points: Use algebraic notation correctly, including indices, fractional coefficients and brackets (A1).
Substitute into expressions and formulae, including scientific formulae (A2).
Use the vocabulary of expressions, equations, formulae, identities, inequalities, terms and factors (A3).
Simplify, expand and factorise; at Higher expand several binomials and factorise ax^2 + bx + c (A4).
Use standard formulae and rearrange to change the subject (A5).
Distinguish equations from identities; at Higher construct algebraic proofs (A6).
Treat expressions as functions; at Higher use inverse and composite functions with f(x) notation (A7).

units.title: Algebra: graphs (linear, quadratic and standard curves)
points: Work with coordinates in all four quadrants (A8).
Plot straight-line graphs; use y = mx + c, parallel lines, and equations from two points (A9).
At Higher identify perpendicular lines and their gradients (A9).
Interpret gradients and intercepts of linear functions graphically and numerically (A10).
Find roots, intercepts and turning points of quadratics; at Higher use completing the square (A11).
Recognise and sketch linear, quadratic, cubic and reciprocal graphs (A12).
At Higher also sketch exponential graphs and sine, cosine and tangent graphs (A12).

units.title: Algebra: Higher graph work and real-life graphs
points: Sketch translations and reflections of a given function (A13, Higher only).
Plot and interpret graphs from real contexts, such as distance-time and velocity-time (A14).
At Higher include reciprocal and exponential graphs in context (A14).
Estimate gradients and areas under non-linear graphs and interpret them, without calculus (A15, Higher only).
Use the equation of a circle centred on the origin and find a tangent at a point (A16, Higher only).

units.title: Algebra: linear and quadratic equations
points: Solve linear equations, including unknowns on both sides and with brackets or fractions (A17).
Approximate solutions to equations using graphs (A17).
Solve quadratics by factorising and estimate roots from graphs (A18).
At Higher also solve quadratics by completing the square and the quadratic formula (A18).

units.title: Algebra: simultaneous equations and iteration
points: Solve two linear simultaneous equations algebraically and graphically (A19).
At Higher solve a linear and a quadratic simultaneous pair algebraically (A19).
Find approximate solutions to equations using iteration (A20, Higher only).

units.title: Algebra: forming equations and inequalities
points: Translate situations into equations, solve them and interpret the solution (A21).
Solve linear inequalities in one variable and show them on a number line (A22).
At Higher cover inequalities in two variables, quadratic inequalities, set notation and regions on graphs (A22).

units.title: Algebra: sequences
points: Generate terms using term-to-term and position-to-term rules (A23).
Recognise triangular, square, cube, arithmetic, Fibonacci-type, quadratic and geometric sequences (A24).
At Higher geometric sequences may have surd ratios (A24).
Find the nth term of linear sequences; at Higher also quadratic sequences (A25).

units.title: Ratio, proportion and rates of change: units, scale and ratio
points: Convert between related standard and compound units in numerical and algebraic contexts (R1).
Use scale factors, scale diagrams and maps (R2).
Write one quantity as a fraction of another, including fractions above 1 (R3).
Use ratio notation, simplify ratios and share in a given ratio (R4, R5).
Express a multiplicative relationship as a ratio or fraction (R6).
Use proportion as equality of ratios and link ratio to fractions and linear functions (R7, R8).

units.title: Ratio, proportion and rates of change: percentages, proportion and compound measures
points: Use percentages above 100%, percentage change, reverse percentages and simple interest (R9).
Solve direct and inverse proportion problems using graphs and algebra (R10).
Use compound units: speed, pay rates, unit pricing, density and pressure (R11).
Compare lengths, areas and volumes using ratio, linked to similarity and scale factors (R12).

units.title: Ratio, proportion and rates of change: proportional equations, rates and growth
points: Understand inverse proportion as X proportional to 1/Y; at Higher construct the equations (R13).
Interpret the gradient of a straight-line graph as a rate of change (R14).
Recognise graphs of direct and inverse proportion (R14).
Interpret the gradient at a point on a curve as an instantaneous rate of change, using tangents (R15, Higher only).
Solve growth and decay problems, including compound interest; at Higher general iterative processes (R16).

units.title: Geometry and measures: properties, constructions and transformations
points: Use geometric vocabulary and notation, and draw diagrams from descriptions (G1).
Use ruler and compass constructions and solve loci problems (G2).
Apply angle facts at a point, on a line, in parallel lines, triangles and polygons (G3).
Use properties of quadrilaterals and other plane figures (G4).
Use congruence criteria SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS (G5).
Use angle, congruence and similarity properties to derive results and simple proofs (G6).
Describe and construct congruent and similar shapes by transformation; at Higher use negative scale factors (G7).
At Higher describe how combinations of rotations, reflections and translations affect shapes (G8).

units.title: Geometry and measures: circles, solids and units
points: Identify and use circle parts: chord, tangent, arc, sector and segment (G9).
Apply and prove standard circle theorems (G10, Higher only).
Solve geometry problems on coordinate axes (G11).
Identify faces, surfaces, edges and vertices of 3D solids (G12).
Construct and interpret plans and elevations of 3D shapes (G13).
Use standard measurement units and related concepts (G14).

units.title: Geometry and measures: measuring, mensuration and similarity
points: Measure lines and angles; use maps, scale drawings and bearings (G15).
Use area formulae for triangles, parallelograms, trapezia, and volume of prisms including cylinders (G16).
Use circle formulae; find surface areas and volumes of spheres, pyramids, cones and composite solids (G17).
Calculate arc lengths, angles and sector areas (G18).
Apply similarity to lengths; at Higher to areas and volumes (G19).

units.title: Geometry and measures: Pythagoras and trigonometry
points: Use Pythagoras and sine, cosine and tangent in right-angled triangles (G20).
At Higher extend Pythagoras and trigonometry to 3D figures (G20).
Know exact trigonometric values for 0, 30, 45, 60 and 90 degrees (G21).
Use the sine rule and cosine rule to find lengths and angles (G22, Higher only).
Use the area formula one half ab sin C for any triangle (G23, Higher only).

units.title: Geometry and measures: vectors
points: Describe translations as 2D column vectors (G24).
Add, subtract and scalar-multiply vectors using diagrams and column notation (G25).
At Higher use vectors in geometric arguments and proofs (G25).

units.title: Probability
points: Record and analyse outcome frequencies using tables and frequency trees (P1).
Use randomness, fairness and equally likely outcomes; link expected frequency to probability (P2, P3).
Know that probabilities of exhaustive, mutually exclusive outcomes sum to 1 (P4).
Understand that larger unbiased samples tend towards the theoretical probability (P5).
List outcomes systematically with tables, grids, Venn diagrams and tree diagrams (P6, P7).
Calculate probabilities of independent and dependent combined events, stating assumptions (P8).
At Higher calculate conditional probabilities using two-way tables, trees and Venn diagrams (P9).

units.title: Statistics
points: Infer properties of a population from samples, recognising limitations of sampling (S1).
Construct and interpret tables, charts and diagrams for categorical, discrete data and time series (S2).
Construct and interpret histograms with unequal class widths and cumulative frequency graphs (S3, Higher only).
Compare distributions using suitable graphs and averages and spread (S4).
At Higher use box plots, quartiles and interquartile range (S4).
Use statistics to describe a population (S5).
Interpret scatter graphs, correlation and lines of best fit, noting the risks of extrapolation (S6).

arabic.subject: Arabic
arabic.framework: National Curriculum in England (2013): Languages programmes of study, key stage 2 (foreign language) and key stage 3 (modern foreign language)
arabic.statusNote: The gov.uk statutory guidance page for the languages programmes of study was opened and summarised; the two programme-of-study PDFs were not separately opened. Arabic is not named in the programmes, but KS2 allows any modern or ancient foreign language and KS3 any modern foreign language. Status Provisional. November 2026 alignment with the school's own Arabic files: Years 7 to 9 follow the Tarbiyyah Secondary KS3 Arabic scheme of work (topic per half term) and the Arabic Curriculum Intent (grammar points, assessments); Years 3 to 6 keep Kitabi (pupils placed by level) with the half-term topics and grammar focus of the Tarbiyyah Primary Year 3 to 6 curriculum maps (2023-24). The founding year teaches Spring 1 to Summer 2 from Mon 11 Jan 2027, after induction week (4 to 8 Jan, no live lessons); Spring 1 weeks 1 and 2 (11 and 18 Jan) are a bridge of the Autumn essentials.
purpose: To give pupils an opening to other languages and cultures.
To help pupils understand and respond to spoken and written language and to communicate for practical purposes.
To speak with growing confidence, write accurately and appreciate the language's writing.
arabic.toKS4: The KS3 scheme feeds the Pearson GCSE Arabic (1AA0) themes in the order the school's GCSE scheme of work teaches them. Y8 About me, My family and Hobbies and Y9 What does he look like? feed Theme 1 Who am I? (1.1) and Cultural life (1.3); Y8 At home and Y9 Food feed Daily life (1.2); Y9 My town and Transport feed Theme 2 Town, region and country (2.3) and Travel (2.2); Y9 Clothes feeds shopping (1.2, 2.2); Y9 At school feeds Theme 3 (3.1); Y8 My job feeds Theme 4 Work (4.3). Y9 Summer 2 ends with an introduction to the GCSE course. The same grammar (agreement, plurals, tenses, imperative, participles) serves 4AA1 Paper 1 grammar.

art.statusNote: Verified from official text read in full: National Curriculum art and design programmes of study (gov.uk, key stages 1 to 3, re-read October 2026); EYFS Expressive Arts and Design and Fine Motor early learning goals (statutory framework from 1 September 2026); DfE GCSE art and design subject content (January 2015). The AQA page is cited only as an example of assessment objectives. Statutory statements are by key stage; the year-by-year allocation is a recommended sequence, not statutory. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment: Years 1 to 6 follow the Tarbiyyah Primary Long Term Plan 2026-27 project order, with content checked against the school's 2023-24 curriculum maps and art and design and DT long-term plans; each Spring 1 to Summer 2 unit carries its week plan, resources and founding-year line.
purpose: Art, craft and design are among humanity's creative achievements and shape history and culture.
Teaching should build skill, experimentation and original work, with deeper critical thinking in older pupils.
Pupils should record ideas, master drawing, painting, sculpture and other techniques, and evaluate work using subject vocabulary.
Pupils should learn about notable artists, craft makers, designers and architects and how their fields developed.
art.toKS4: Key stage 3 prepares pupils for GCSE Art and Design, where the four assessment objectives are, in general terms: develop ideas through investigation informed by sources (AO1); refine work by experimenting with media and processes (AO2); record ideas and observations (AO3); present a personal, informed outcome (AO4). In the AQA GCSE example opened, each objective carries 25% across a portfolio (60%) and an externally set assignment (40%). Year 9 sketchbook, drawing, design and research units build those habits. The school's GCSE board and endorsement are not confirmed, so no unit references are given. The DfE GCSE subject content (January 2015, read in full) requires drawing to support development in every area of study, allows entirely digital or non-digital work, and lists seven titles: art, craft and design; fine art; graphic communication; textile design; three-dimensional design; photography; critical and contextual studies. Year 7 to 9 units on sketchbooks, drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture, textiles, photography and digital work map to these titles.

computing.subject: Computing
computing.framework: National Curriculum in England (2014): Computing programmes of study (Key Stages 1 to 3), with an early-years technology foundation for Reception
computing.statusNote: Key stage statements were read and paraphrased from the gov.uk National Curriculum computing programmes of study. The EYFS statutory framework (September 2026 version) has no technology-specific early learning goal, so the Reception year map is a recommended early-skills sequence, not statutory content. Statutory content is set by key stage, not by year; the year allocation is a recommended sequence aligned to the school's existing unit names. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment with the school's own files: Years 1 to 6 follow the Tarbiyyah Primary computing scheme of work (2022-23; Years 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 partly filled in, Year 2 blank templates) and computing long-term plan (2023-24), which are built on the NCCE Teach Computing Curriculum (a publisher's generic scheme) with an e-awareness lesson at the start of units and named online-safety lessons. Years 3 to 6 are taught in Autumn 1, Spring 1 and Summer 1 only. Not adopted: Making Music (Year 2) and the music content of Sequencing Sounds (Year 3).
purpose: Computing education builds computational thinking and creativity, with links to mathematics, science, and design and technology.
It rests on three strands: computer science, information technology and digital literacy.
Pupils learn to write programs, solve problems by breaking them into parts, and understand how computers work.
Pupils become responsible, confident and creative users of digital technology.
computing.toKS4: Key Stage 3 prepares pupils for Pearson Edexcel GCSE Computer Science 1CP2 (Paper 1 Topics 1 to 5, Paper 2 Topic 6 in Python 3). Algorithms, flowcharts, searching and sorting set up Topic 1 (1.1 to 1.3). Binary, data representation and file sizes set up Topic 2. Hardware, software and translators set up Topic 3. Networks and protocols set up Topic 4. Online safety, ethics, law and the environment set up Topic 5. Scratch then Python, with functions, lists and strings, set up Topic 6 (6.1 to 6.6), which is assessed by an on-screen programming exam.

english.subject: English
english.framework: National Curriculum in England (2014): English programmes of study, Key Stages 1 to 3, with EYFS Literacy and Communication and Language for Reception
english.statusNote: All content was compared with the official text, read as raw text from the gov.uk and assets.publishing.service.gov.uk PDFs listed in sources: the primary (KS1-2) and secondary (KS3) English programmes of study, Appendix 1 (spelling), Appendix 2 (vocabulary, grammar and punctuation), the glossary (used to check terminology) and the EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers (dated 13 July 2026, effective 1 September 2026): the Communication and Language, Literacy and Fine Motor sections and Early Learning Goals. EYFS assessment and welfare sections were not needed for this syllabus. The statutory content is set by key stage (Year 1 and Year 2 individually in KS1; two-year blocks in KS2; KS3 as one block); the year-by-year allocation, the phonics order in Reception and Year 1, and the chosen texts (The Explorer, war poetry, Of Mice and Men, and similar) are the school's recommended sequence, not statutory. Spelling and grammar are recorded at topic level in paraphrase; the Year 3-4 and Year 5-6 statutory word lists are named, not reproduced. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment: Years 1 to 6 follow the Tarbiyyah Primary English schemes of work (one per Cornerstones project, the school's own adaptation of the Cornerstones English units) for texts, writing outcomes and order; projects with no school scheme among the files (Year 1 Splendid Skies, Year 4 Road Trip USA, Year 5 Scream Machine, Stargazers, Alchemy Island and Ground-Breaking Greeks, Year 6 ID) use the text types in the school's curriculum maps. Texts the school may find unsuitable are flagged TO CONFIRM, not swapped silently.
purpose: English is essential to education: pupils must speak, read and write fluently to take part in society.
Reading, especially literature, supports cultural, emotional, intellectual, social and spiritual development.
Pupils should write clearly for different audiences, and use discussion to learn and explain ideas.
Pupils build a wide vocabulary, understand grammar and conventions, and appreciate the literary heritage.
english.toKS4: KS3 reading, writing, grammar and spoken English prepare pupils for AQA GCSE English Language 8700 and English Literature 8702. For Language, Paper 1 (Explorations in Creative Reading and Writing: AO1, AO2, AO4 reading; AO5, AO6 writing) and Paper 2 (Writers' Viewpoints and Perspectives: AO1, AO2, AO3 reading; AO5, AO6 writing) each carry 80 marks and 50%; the Spoken Language endorsement (AO7 to AO9) is reported separately. For Literature, Paper 1 (Shakespeare and the 19th-century novel: 64 marks, 40%) and Paper 2 (Modern texts and poetry: 96 marks, 60%) assess AO1 to AO4. KS3 inference and evidence feed AO1, language and structure analysis feeds AO2, comparison of poems and viewpoints feeds AO3 (Language) and Literature's poetry comparison, context feeds Literature AO3, and the writing and grammar thread feeds AO5, AO6 and Literature AO4. The KS3 requirement for two Shakespeare plays and pre-1914 literature leads to the Paper 1 set texts.

geography.subject: Geography
geography.framework: National Curriculum in England (2014): Geography programmes of study, Key Stages 1 to 3, with EYFS Understanding the World
geography.statusNote: Verified from official text: National Curriculum geography programmes of study for key stages 1 to 3 (gov.uk, re-read October 2026) and the EYFS Understanding the World early learning goals (People, Culture and Communities; The Natural World) in the statutory framework from 1 September 2026, read in full text. The Reception unit now follows those goals. Year allocation is a recommended sequence, not statutory; the National Curriculum sets content by key stage. Year units follow the school's existing unit titles. School-choice notes, not verification gaps: KS1 contrasting-country place knowledge, KS2 Europe and North America, KS3 Africa and Asia, KS3 locational knowledge, development and economic sectors, geological time, weather and climate have no matching school units yet; online pupils need a route for fieldwork (for example guided local fieldwork with a parent or tutor). Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment: Years 1 to 6 keep the Tarbiyyah Primary Long Term Plan 2026-27 project order, with each project's geography content taken from the school's 2023-24 curriculum maps and geography long-term plan; fieldwork is done at home or online.
purpose: Spark lasting curiosity about the world, its places, people and environments.
Understand the physical and human processes that shape places and how they interconnect.
Gather, analyse and communicate geographical information through maps, fieldwork, data and extended writing.
geography.toKS4: KS3 sets up AQA 8035 as follows. Y4 Restless Earth and Y9 climate and sustainability lead to 3.1.1 natural hazards and climate change; Y5 Amazon leads to 3.1.2 the living world; Y3 rivers, Y7 Lake District landscape and Y8 coasts lead to 3.1.3 physical landscapes; Y7 UK population and cities lead to 3.2.1 urban issues; Y9 resources, energy and sustainability lead to 3.2.3 resource management; Y8 and Y9 decision-making tasks lead to 3.3.1 issue evaluation; OS and data skills lead to 3.4 skills and 3.3.2 fieldwork. National Curriculum KS3 development and economic sectors are covered thinly in current units and feed 3.2.2.

history.subject: History
history.framework: National Curriculum in England (2014): History programmes of study, Key Stages 1 to 3, with EYFS Understanding the World
history.statusNote: Key Stage 1 to 3 statutory content and period lists were re-read from the gov.uk National Curriculum history programme of study (page read through a fetch tool that returns summaries, checked against the earlier reading). EYFS Understanding the World: Past and Present was read in the 13 July 2026 statutory framework (in force 1 September 2026) and the Reception row matches it. Year allocation is a recommended sequence, not statutory; the National Curriculum sets content by key stage. Year units follow the school's existing unit titles. History is taught from Year 1 to Year 9 only; it is not offered at Key Stage 4. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment: Years 1 to 6 keep the Tarbiyyah Primary Long Term Plan 2026-27 project order, with each project's history content taken from the school's 2023-24 curriculum maps and history long-term plan (for example Year 3 Mighty Metals teaches the History of Sports Tournaments, as in the map).
purpose: Build coherent knowledge of Britain and the wider world and spark curiosity about the past.
Use evidence, interpretations and second-order concepts such as change, cause, similarity and significance.
Link local, national and international history across short and long timescales.
history.toKS4: History is not offered at Key Stage 4: the subject ends in Year 9. The KS3 skills carry into other KS4 subjects: chronology, cause and consequence and source analysis into Islamic Studies (4IS1 Section A, the life of the Prophet and the early Muslim community); context and interpretation into English Literature (4ET1 AO4, for example Jacobean England for Macbeth and 1930s America for Of Mice and Men); and change over time into Geography (development and urban change). Pupils who want GCSE History later can build on the Year 7 to Year 9 units.

islamic-studies.subject: Islamic Studies
islamic-studies.framework: Statutory RE entitlement (no National Curriculum programme of study); the school's own Islamic Studies programme
islamic-studies.statusNote: There is no National Curriculum programme of study for RE, so this is the school's own programme, taken from its lesson files (content/lessons/islamic-studies, Reception to Year 9) and the Ibn Baz course plan in the school Drive. The gov.uk RE page was opened but says nothing about independent schools. Year allocation is a recommended sequence. Status Provisional. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one.
purpose: To know Allah, the Prophet and the faith of Islam through creed, worship and character.
To practise worship correctly and live by Islamic manners at home, school and online.
To build the knowledge and skills needed for the Edexcel International GCSE Islamic Studies course.
islamic-studies.toKS4: The KS3 programme feeds the Edexcel International GCSE Islamic Studies (4IS1) sections. Section A (Prophet's life): Y7 Makkan seerah supports 1.1 to 1.4, Y8 Madinah and Badr support 1.4 and 1.8, Y9 Hudaybiyyah, Conquest and Farewell Sermon support 1.7 and 1.9, Y7 and Y9 hadith units support 1.5. Section B (beliefs): Y7 to Y9 aqidah and iman units support 2.1 to 2.6, Y8 sources of law supports 2.7, Y8 to Y9 akhlaq supports 2.8. Section C (living the Muslim life): fiqh of worship, zakah, sawm and Hajj support 3.2 to 3.5. The Ibn Baz supplementary course supports 2.1 (tawhid and shirk), 3.2 (prayer and wudu) and 2.8 (character) but does NOT cover the Prophet's life (1.1 to 1.9) or the early community (2.9). Also not yet covered: Muhammad's role in justice (1.6), Prophet as leader (1.7) in depth, the earlier prophets Musa, Dawud, Isa (2.2), jihad (3.6), festivals (3.7), marriage and family (3.8) and citizenship (3.9).

mathematics.framework: National Curriculum in England (2014): Mathematics programmes of study, with EYFS Mathematics (Number; Numerical Patterns) for Reception
mathematics.statusNote: Key stage statements were read and paraphrased from the gov.uk National Curriculum mathematics programmes of study (Key Stages 1 to 3) and the Reception goals from the EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers (version effective September 2026). Statutory content is set by key stage, not by year. The year allocation in the year map is a recommended sequence aligned to the school's existing unit names, not a statutory requirement. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment: Years 1 to 6 follow the Tarbiyyah Primary Long Term Plan 2026-27 project order, with content checked against the school's 2023-24 curriculum maps and maths long-term plan and Maths policy (White Rose); each Spring 1 to Summer 2 unit carries its week plan, resources and founding-year line.
purpose: Mathematics is a creative, connected discipline used in daily life, science, engineering, finance and work.
Pupils become fluent, with quick and accurate recall of core mathematics.
Pupils reason mathematically: conjecture, generalise, justify and prove.
Pupils solve routine and unfamiliar problems by breaking them into steps and persevering.
mathematics.toKS4: Key Stage 3 prepares pupils for Pearson Edexcel GCSE Mathematics 1MA1 (Higher tier at the school). Number: place value, powers, roots, standard form and fractions set up N1 to N16. Algebra: notation, expanding, factorising, linear graphs and sequences set up A1 to A25. Ratio, proportion and rates of change: ratio, percentage change, direct proportion and compound units set up R1 to R16. Geometry and measures: angle facts, area, volume, constructions, Pythagoras and trigonometry set up G1 to G25. Probability: sample spaces and Venn diagrams set up P1 to P9. Statistics: averages, charts and scatter graphs set up S1 to S6. Year 9 introduces quadratics, standard form, trigonometry and tree diagrams so that Year 10 can begin the 1MA1 content at pace.

pshe.subject: PSHE
pshe.framework: Statutory guidance: Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) and Health Education (revised, in force from 1 September 2026); National Curriculum in England: Citizenship programmes of study KS3 and KS4; PSHE Association programme of study (non-statutory reference); EYFS PSED for Reception. School position: PSHE only in every year group, with no RSE or sex education; puberty and bulugh taught from Year 7 to boys and girls separately
pshe.statusNote: Provisional. Read in full text from official sources: the 1 September 2026 RSHE statutory guidance PDF, compared line by line with the July 2025 PDF (the two extracts are identical; the 2026 file is the July 2025 text reissued); National Curriculum citizenship KS3 and KS4 (official PDF); the EYFS PSED goals (framework from 1 September 2026); the gov.uk collection page. The DfE will not publish standalone gender-questioning guidance: it proposes to put that content in Keeping children safe in education (policy paper, 12 February 2026), so nothing separate exists to read. Not verified: the PSHE Association programme of study download (learning opportunities by key stage), which could not be opened in October 2026; its core themes (Health and wellbeing, Relationships, Living in the wider world) come from earlier reads of site pages. Year allocation is a recommended sequence. School decisions recorded (October 2026, updated 26 October): the subject is PSHE only in every year group, with no RSE or sex education (manners, friendships, families, health and hygiene, and keeping safe, including body safety at a non-sexual level and what the law says to protect young people); puberty and bulugh are taught from Year 7 to boys and girls separately; parents can see all PSHE materials. Statements below quote the national guidance; the school's lessons follow these decisions. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment: Years 1 to 6 follow Tarbiyyah Primary's PSHE scheme of work and PSHE long-term plan (the Ealing LA PSHE, Citizenship and SEAL spiral scheme, a local-authority scheme: Year A units in Years 1, 3, 5 and Year B units in Years 2, 4, 6), with every RSE and puberty lesson left out, theme weeks and festival dates not adopted, and fund-raising adapted to a sadaqah plan at home.
purpose: PSHE helps pupils stay safe and healthy and form respectful relationships, taught within an Islamic ethos.
Primary pupils (Years 1 to 6): adab, friendships, families, health, hygiene and keeping safe, including body safety. The subject is PSHE only.

Secondary pupils (Years 7 to 11): PSHE taught from an Islamic perspective, with puberty and bulugh taught to boys and girls separately: marriage and family, modesty, puberty and its fiqh, consent and the law, online harms and mental wellbeing.
Citizenship prepares pupils to take an active part in society, including democracy, law, rights and personal finance.
pshe.toKS4: Years 10 and 11 continue PSHE (taught from an Islamic perspective, with puberty and bulugh taught to boys and girls separately) and add National Curriculum KS4 citizenship content (law, rights, democracy and personal finance). School content for Years 10 and 11 already covers stress, relationships and the law, gambling and exploitation, work, post-16 pathways, money, first aid, and consent, modesty and the law. There is no examination in this programme and no board unit references. Key stage 3 builds the vocabulary, safe-help habits and legal awareness these units extend.

quran.statusNote: No National Curriculum or exam-board framework exists for Qur'an and Tajweed. This is the school's own programme, drawn from its lesson files (Reception to Year 9) and the tajweed-by-year layout of the old Drive Quran tracker. Recitation follows the Madinah mushaf, Hafs 'an 'Asim. Year allocation is a recommended sequence. Status Provisional. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one.
purpose: To read the Qur'an fluently and accurately from the mushaf with correct tajweed.
To memorise selected surahs securely and keep them through revision.
To understand the meaning of what is recited and to show adab with the Qur'an.
Standard: Arabic script is always shown with transliteration, never transliteration alone.
quran.toKS4: There is no Qur'an qualification at KS4 in this pack. Year 10 and 11 lesson files continue the programme (Ayat al-Kursi 2:255, Surat Al-Mulk 67:1-4, Surat Al-Kahf 18:1-10) and support Edexcel International GCSE Islamic Studies (4IS1), whose set passages (for example 97:1-5, 112:1-4, 2:183-185) are studied in Arabic and English. Qur'an lessons give recitation and meaning for these passages in sections 1.2, 2.1 and 3.3.

science.subject: Science
science.framework: National Curriculum in England (2014): Science programmes of study (Key Stages 1 to 3); Reception aligned to EYFS Understanding the World: The Natural World
science.statusNote: Key Stage 1, 2 and 3 statements were read from the gov.uk National Curriculum science programme of study; the whole page, including the end of the Key Stage 4 section, has now been read, and a sample of Year 2 to Year 6 statements was re-checked against the official primary PDF with no errors found. EYFS Understanding the World: The Natural World was read in the 13 July 2026 statutory framework (in force 1 September 2026) and the Reception row is consistent with it. Statutory content is set by key stage and by named year for KS1 and KS2; the Year 7 to Year 9 allocation and all unit titles are a recommended sequence because the National Curriculum sets Key Stage 3 content as a whole. Pages were read through a fetch tool that summarises text. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment: Years 1 to 6 follow the Tarbiyyah Primary Long Term Plan 2026-27 project order, with content checked against the school's 2023-24 curriculum maps and science long-term plan; each Spring 1 to Summer 2 unit carries its week plan, resources and founding-year line.
purpose: Science builds understanding of the world through biology, chemistry and physics, with core knowledge, methods and uses.
Pupils develop key concepts that spark curiosity and help them explain, predict and analyse causes.
Pupils learn how scientific enquiry works so they can judge science's uses and implications now and later.
Precise technical vocabulary is expected, and schools may teach content earlier or later within a key stage.
science.toKS4: KS3 sets up the Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9-1) sciences: cells, organs and digestion lead to Biology Topics 1 and 2; variation, DNA and natural selection lead to Biology Topics 3 and 4; photosynthesis, respiration, ecosystems and plants lead to Biology Topics 6, 8 and 9. Particle model, separation, atoms, reactions and the periodic table feed Chemistry Topics 1 to 4 and 6; combustion, atmosphere and climate feed Chemistry Topic 8. Forces and motion, energy, waves, electricity, magnetism and space feed Physics Topics 2 to 5, 7 to 10 and 12 to 15. Working scientifically feeds all core practicals and AO3.
